title: Revenue Engineering: How to Price (and Reprice) Your AI Product — Kshitij Grover, Orb
talk_summary: The speaker explains AI product pricing principles: audience, margin structure, flexibility, and frequent repricing. He recommends guardrails, model switching, usage simulation, and spend visibility to manage variable AI costs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Protect margins by using rate limits or guardrails to discourage unreasonable usage rather than linearly absorbing every cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you incentivize reasonable usage? you put in rate limits or guardrails.

takeaways.technique: Automatic model switching under the hood
takeaways.what_they_do: Route between models seamlessly so users do not have to pick the right model for each job.
takeaways.evidence_quote: switch between models under the hood seamlessly. You don't have to choose the right model for the job.

takeaways.technique: Simulate quota/pricing changes on historical usage
takeaways.what_they_do: Before changing pricing, simulate impact across user cohorts and usage patterns using data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: simulate the impact that this pricing change is going to have on your users

takeaways.technique: Real-time spend visibility and balance alerts
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide live visibility into spend and alerts so teams can manage usage before budgets are exhausted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: real-time visibility, spend management, uh balance alerts.

takeaways.what_they_do: Have the agent present execution plans with estimated credit/token cost so the user can choose a cheaper path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: here's three options for um how I might execute... One's going to take 10,000 credits, the other's going to take, you know, 4,000 credits.
